high_value_findings.finding: SOMA is not merely LoRA training: it is a recurrent control loop over interaction selection, explicit feedback, quality scoring, scheduled training, safety gates, EMA deployment, hot reload, rollback and runtime configuration. Multiple audit rounds found concurrency, stale-config, TOCTOU, dropped-parameter, thread and memory-leak failures.
high_value_findings.transfer: Treat online adaptation as a safety-critical state machine with explicit transaction boundaries, single-writer training leases, deterministic rollback, class-balance telemetry and fault-injection tests; model-quality metrics alone are insufficient.

high_value_findings.finding: Thumbs feedback became the strongest scorer signal and later weighted training strongly, including explicit negative-example handling. This improves preference responsiveness but also makes user rating behavior a direct model-update actuator.
high_value_findings.transfer: Separate preference reward from factual/capability/safety objectives; log provenance, calibration and class balance, cap influence, and evaluate Goodhart/overfit under sparse, adversarial or inconsistent feedback.

high_value_findings.finding: Personality change was visualized from five sampled prompts and lexical/style heuristics; subsequent audits fixed substring false positives, failure averaging and defaults. Sampling remained stochastic and dimensions are operational proxies.
high_value_findings.transfer: Do not interpret radar/change percentages as latent personality ground truth. Use fixed seeds or repeated samples, confidence intervals, held-out behavioral tasks and probe-invariance tests before promotion.

high_value_findings.finding: Memory retrieval was redesigned around entity-vector removal, stop-word FTS, relevance-dominant scoring, maturity gates, graph-expansion suppression and HNSW; the commit reports P@5 improvement from 0.40 to 1.00.
high_value_findings.transfer: Preserve the exact retrieval benchmark/query set and reproduce across fresh/OOD queries; isolate each intervention with ablations before attributing the gain to HNSW or neural retrieval.

high_value_findings.finding: Nightly autonomous news collection was deliberately removed while Intelligence V6 moved to user-triggered/on-demand search, crawl and synthesis with relevance/drift/claim-dedup guards.
high_value_findings.transfer: Autonomy should be budgeted per task value and contamination risk; scheduled background collection is not inherently superior to demand-driven retrieval and must justify storage, freshness and failure costs.

high_value_findings.finding: A separate RSS feed ranker used a tiny neural model and direct click/dismiss feedback without LLM calls.
high_value_findings.transfer: Prefer small task-specific adaptive models where the objective is narrow and observable; benchmark them against LLM-based personalization for latency, energy, interpretability and feedback sample efficiency.

high_value_findings.finding: Core architecture, installer, model paths, native vision and SOMA training were migrated across Qwen generations while old components/models were removed. The changes couple runtime, training artifacts, deployment and safety filters.
high_value_findings.transfer: Model migration requires an explicit compatibility matrix for base model, LoRA adapter, tokenizer, GGUF/HF paths, prompt format, tool policy and deployment backend; partial migration can silently corrupt behavior.

negative_results_preserved: SOMA runtime configuration could remain stale after WebUI changes.
Concurrent forced/background training could corrupt shared adapter outputs without a run lock.
Restart flags had a check-then-unlink TOCTOU race.
EMA blending silently omitted new adapter keys before union-key handling.
Training error paths leaked large model objects and background toggles leaked threads.
Personality probe substring matching and failed-probe averaging produced false measurement shifts.
A zero-norm baseline could be incorrectly judged as zero drift.
Nightly autonomous news collection was removed rather than retained as inherently useful autonomy.
LCME retrieval had sufficiently poor historical precision that a later commit reports P@5 0.40 before redesign.
epistemic_boundary: SOMA change percentages are heuristic sampled behavior metrics, not direct measurements of identity/personality. The reported SOMA training runtime/sample counts and LCME P@5 improvement are preserved as historical measurements/claims and require benchmark artifact reproduction before scientific promotion. Project consciousness/personality wording in prompts/docs is not phenomenal-consciousness evidence.

earned_work.reason: No row-level conceptual dedup against the earned-work ledger was performed.

next_falsifiers: Run crash/concurrency fault injection across SOMA score->train->validate->EMA->convert->reload->rollback transitions with exactly-once deployment assertions.
Simulate sparse, all-positive, all-negative, contradictory and adversarial thumbs feedback; measure adapter drift, factual accuracy, safety and preference overfit separately.
Repeat personality probes over multiple deterministic seeds and held-out prompts; quantify variance and correlation with human-rated behavioral dimensions.
Reproduce LCME P@5 on the frozen query corpus and fresh OOD queries, then ablate stop words, vector cleanup, graph expansion, maturity gates, scoring and HNSW independently.
Model-migration matrix test: base HF/GGUF/tokenizer/LoRA compatibility plus hot-reload and rollback across CPU/Vulkan/GPU paths.
Compare tiny feed ranker versus LLM reranking under matched feedback on relevance, diversity, energy, latency and sample efficiency.
Compare scheduled autonomous intelligence collection against on-demand retrieval on freshness, contamination, storage growth, latency and user-value metrics.
